plain_english_revision: The amendment modifies qualifications for school resource officers (SROs) by removing vague language, adding a requirement for youth-focused training, and restricting arrest authority to certified officers. It also clarifies that retired law enforcement may qualify as SROs.
candidate_position_supported: Advances a policy of **standardizing and restricting** the authority of school resource officers by requiring specialized youth training, limiting arrest powers to certified personnel, and clarifying eligibility criteria for retired officers.
evidence_quotes: qualified under this section or retired law enforcement officers
has received specialized training to work with youth at a school site
Only those school resource officers who are certified by the Alabama Peace Officers' Standards and Training Commission shall have the power of arrest
review_reason: The amendment's intent is clear from its explicit deletions/insertions, though broader context (e.g., original bill text) would confirm whether this reflects a shift toward stricter oversight or procedural clarification.
